alternatives.argument: The local proof constructs the form resolvent by Riesz representation on the shifted complete form domain, proves positivity and injectivity, inverts it by Borel calculus, and identifies both the operator domain and uniqueness. Porta Theorem 4.65 is an independent interface check; the local argument supplies the complete proof.

The local proof derives the variational values by spectral-projection rank comparisons, treats finite and empty essential-spectrum thresholds, and proves the compact form embedding conclusion through the shifted resolvent and compact spectral theorem. Teschl Theorem 4.9 and LMU §2.3 are inspected independent treatments.

The local proof factors the rank-one resolvent through X=R0 P_g, proves X²=mX, multiplies the proposed inverse on both sides on the operator domain, and derives both directions and eigenspace dimension of the below-threshold scalar equation. Teschl Problem 6.1 supplies the independent resolvent identity check.

alternatives.argument: The complete local proof uses spectral-projection rank comparisons, verifies the finite and empty essential-spectrum cases, and derives the compact-embedding result through a compact shifted resolvent and the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem. The LMU §2.3 lecture-note proof is an independent check.

The complete local proof establishes self-adjointness by a bounded symmetric perturbation, verifies the proposed inverse on both sides through X²=mX, and proves both directions of the below-threshold eigenvalue criterion. Albeverio and Kurasov Theorem 1.1.1 supplies an independent full rank-one resolvent proof.

The complete local proof identifies the weak-derivative form by Fourier transform, proves closedness and density, and identifies the represented operator domain as W^{2,2}. The LMU §2.5 free Schrödinger realization is an independent check.

The complete local proof integrates the radial Fourier transform, verifies L¹ and L² integrability, proves the convolution multiplier identity by density, and identifies the resolvent. The LMU §3.3 notes independently record the three-dimensional Fourier-side kernel.
